To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) A simple distributed inductance capacitance resistance (DLCR), channel model of lightning is sufficient to model lightning return stroke currents and electromagnetic fields; 2) A DLCR channel model of long arcs in electric power transmission lines is sufficient to model the high frequency transients generated by long arcs.
the lightning return stroke model is based on a fundamentally straightforward distributed circuit model and that the wave guide model of the return stroke is not justified.

a fundamentally straightforward DCR model captures all measured lightning return stroke characteristics, that the waveguide lightning model makes assumptions that can be scientifically unjustified, and that a new arc model can be used to improve the quality of power delivered to consumers in PNG and elsewhere.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing models of lightning and arcs in order to improve the quality of the power supply to consumers in Papua New Guinea, and to increase the reliability and efficiency of power transmission in the nation.
the development of new methods to model the lightning channel and arcs in electric power networks.
improving power quality to PNG consumers and to the nation as a whole.

the model presented here is an improvement on the state-of-art and that it will be a major contribution to the field.
a simple and straightforward distributed model of the lightning return strike channel and the high voltage long arcs can be used to accurately predict lightning and high voltage long arc behavior.
the model proposed in this paper is a major step forward to improve the quality of the power grid in PNG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lightning channel model has been extended to high voltage arc models and a new model has been proposed to improve the quality of the national electricity network.
the lightning model is a reliable and accurate representation of the electromagnetic phenomena that characterizes it and can be used to predict its effects.

we have been able to model the lightning return stroke and the electric arc using a distributed inductance, capacitance, resistance (DLCR), and the waveguide models, and that we have developed a model for the electric arc which captures the high frequency components that generate power surges that impact electronic and communication devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of power delivered to consumers can be greatly improved by a better understanding of the electric arc.
the quality of the power network can be improved by using a new model of the electric arc.

the electric arc is a major source of power surges that impacts the quality of the electricity delivered to consumers and that a better understanding of the arc is required to improve the quality of electricity delivered to consumers.
